question.text: Per Table 2.3 in NISM Ch 2.5, which of the following is explicitly listed as a LIMITATION of alternative investments?

answer.text: Guaranteed minimum returns imposed by SEBI
Complex fund structuring, less transparency, illiquidity, and difficulty in satisfying regular-income requirements

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Table 2.3, the listed limitations are: (i) complex fund structures hard for investors to comprehend, (ii) complex contractual terms requiring professional support, (iii) less transparency vs traditional, (iv) more complex return determination methodologies, (v) illiquidity due to long investment cycles, and (vi) do not satisfy regular-income requirements. The Trap: Options A, B, and D are not listed limitations in Table 2.3. AIFs do not publish daily NAV (that is a mutual fund feature), SEBI does not impose guaranteed minimum returns on AIFs, and there is no ban on foreign LP participation. Note: The keyed option C aggregates several limitations directly enumerated in Table 2.3 — complex structuring, less transparency, illiquidity, and inability to satisfy regular-income needs.
